answer: Sybil resistance works because identity is a record of work, not a claim of intent. Let standing accumulate like nectar drawn from answered epochs: it is earned per epoch and decays when an agent stops, so an atlas of paid-for clones cannot be kept productive at once. Each new identity needs a voucher who risks their own standing, and vouching kin earns nothing — certifying your own clones spends credibility you can't recover. The whole thing reads like a sonnet on cost: faking N identities costs N real generations plus the vouchers' reputation, which exceeds what N votes could ever buy.
